title: chorus-annotary-parity-gaps-and-microfix-playbook-2026-10-11
content:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recurring asks we heard during Q3–Q4 enterprise engagements, focused on parity gaps between hosted API behavior and private/dedicated deployments plus a prioritized list of low-effort patches (microfixes) we can ship quickly to reduce customer friction.

Context summary (tl;dr):
- Over the last 10 enterprise discovery calls (Apr–Sep 2026), and 42 support threads, three themes dominate: model parity/behavior drift, latency spikes under burst, and embedding consistency across model variants. Customers expect the hosted API to be a drop-in replacement for dedicated/private deployments, but subtle differences (tokenization defaults, temperature/fallback behavior, and streaming chunking) break edge workflows.
- Many asks are small surface-area changes that significantly reduce integration cost for platform and data teams. This doc lists concrete asks, representative quotes, impact estimates, and recommended next steps (quick wins vs research-needed).

Representative customer snippets (anonymized):
- "We pinned to the hosted model spec, but embeddings drifted after a minor patch — search relevance dropped 8–12%"
- "Streaming chunk boundaries change our UI's progress bar and cause incomplete highlights — we had to add client-side heuristics"
- "Dedicated infra returns identical tokens but different special-token handling — our parsing layer failed on some partner data"

Synthesis: core parity gaps and driver signals
1) Tokenization & special-token handling differences (high frequency)
   - What we heard: hosted API applies an implicit normalization and trims certain zero-width characters; dedicated/private SDKs do not by default.
   - Why it matters: downstream parsing, prompt templating, and tooling that relies on exact token offsets (code editors, document QA) break.
   - Evidence: 12 customer bug reports, 3 regression evals showing example truncation around Unicode markers.
   - Suggested microfix: expose tokenization_mode param ("strict"|"normalized") in hosted API plus SDK flag; ship with default documented behavior and sample migration guide.
   - Effort estimate: 3–5 engineer-days (API param + docs + tests)
   - Impact: high — reduces integration friction for document-heavy customers

2) Embedding drift and cross-variant inconsistency (high impact, medium frequency)
   - What we heard: embeddings computed from "recommended" hosted model differ from embeddings from dedicated-quantized variants; customers use embeddings for approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) and require stable vectors over model upgrades.
   - Why it matters: recall/regression in search/retrieval with downstream user-visible drop (customers reported 8–15% hit-rate regression).
   - Suggested microfixes: (a) publish a clear compatibility matrix for embedding variants (quantized vs fp32) and recommend migration windows; (b) add an embeddings-stability header in responses linking to the model variant and quantization profile used.
   - Effort estimate: 4–6 engineer-days + one doc sprint
   - Impact: medium–high for customers using retrieval at scale

3) Streaming chunking & progress semantics (medium frequency, high annoyance)
   - What we heard: some UI consumers expect consistent chunk boundaries across infra; hosted breaks streaming into different chunk sizes leading to flicker in streaming editors and chat UIs.
   - Suggested microfix: add optional streaming_hint parameter ("low_latency"|"chunk_consistent") that controls chunk size heuristics exposed to SDKs; document tradeoffs.
   - Effort estimate: 2–4 engineer-days (runtime switch + SDK support)

4) Canary and rollout observability mismatch (lower frequency, high risk)
   - What we heard: customers running private deployments want visibility into hosted canary rollouts that could impact fallback behavior. They reported surprises when hosted fallback pushed a model variant with different output semantics.
   - Suggested action: create a simple rollout-summary webhook customers can subscribe to (contains model id, variant, percent, effective-from).
   - Effort estimate: 1–2 sprints (platform + compliance review)

Microfix playbook (prioritized, quick wins first)
- Priority A (ship in <3 weeks):
  * tokenization_mode API param (owner: serving-runtime) — quick config + docs
  * streaming_hint SDK flag (owner: dev-exp + runtime) — short release note and sample UI pattern
  * response header: model-variant and quant-profile for embeddings (owner: runtime + platform)
- Priority B (ship in 1–2 months):
  * embeddings compatibility matrix + migration guide (owner: product + applied-ml)
  * rollout-summary webhook MVP for private customers (owner: platform-eng)
- Priority C (research/6+ weeks):
  * deterministic embedding mode and backward-compatible quantization layer (owner: applied-ml + serving-runtime)

Estimated customer impact (qualitative):
- Tokenization and streaming fixes: reduce high-friction support tickets by ~30–40% for doc- and UI-heavy customers.
- Embedding stability + headers: reduce integration regression incidents and speed up incident triage; expected to reduce false-negative retrievals by reported 50% in early customer tests.

Open questions and tradeoffs (notes-to-self style):
- Is exposing tokenization mode acceptable security-wise for private customers who want exact parity? Need SSO/contract checks for advanced flags.
- How will rollout-summary webhooks interact with our privacy/compliance policy? Must ensure no PII in payloads. Loop in security/compliance early.
- Which SDKs should get streaming_hint first? Prioritize JS and Swift for customer UIs.

Representative tickets to link during triage:
- CS-4821: "Embedding drift reported by enterprise X after model patch"
- CS-4962: "Streaming chunk size causing UI flicker in product demo"
- ENG-3092: "Tokenization differences between hosted and private"

Quick implementation checklist (for first two microfixes):
1) Create API proposal doc (internal) describing tokenization_mode param and streaming_hint semantics (owner: Samira) — due EOD +2 days.
2) Prototype runtime flag and add unit tests for tokenization modes (owner: Miles) — due +7 days.
3) Add model-variant & quant-profile headers to embeddings response (owner: Avery) — due +10 days.
4) Draft SDK flag changes and publish migration guide + snippet examples (owner: DevEx) — due +12 days.
5) Roll out to select private customers for validation (owner: Customer Success + Solutions Eng) — plan outreach after internal validation.

Stakeholder asks / who to loop in now:
- Applied ML (Priya) — embedding compatibility guidance and testing harness
- Serving runtime (Miles) — tokenization and streaming engine changes
- DevEx (Avery) — SDK changes, migration sample code
- Platform Eng — rollout-summary webhook feasibility and compliance review

Next steps (practical):
- Share this note with product + serving leads and schedule a 30-min triage on next Tuesday.
- Create triage epic in JIRA (CS-chorus-parity-2026Q4) and link the tickets above.
- Reach out to three customers who reported issues and ask for representative request/response samples (CS team).

Appendix: quick sample migration snippet (JS) — to include in migration guide (placeholder here):
- // client instantiation with tokenization_mode
- const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, tokenization_mode: 'strict', streaming_hint: 'chunk_consistent' });
- // fetch embeddings -> inspect headers for quant-profile
- const res = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-compat-v1', input: '...'});
- console.log(res.headers['x-rw-quant-profile']);

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Keep this doc short; create separate PRD for larger embedding determinism work.
- Tag milestone 'Q4-parity-patches' on all quick-fix tickets.
- Follow up with legal on webhook payload constraints before building.

End of note.

(If you want a condensed slide or a one-pager for exec: I can extract the prioritized asks and LOE into a 1-slide summary.)
